page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dlsv6 series, configured with 48 virtual CPUs mapped across 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides dedicated vCPU allocation alongside 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor features 260 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and VAES. No local storage is attached, requiring workloads to rely on remote Azure Premium Storage. There are no onboard graphics processing units.

Benchmark results indicate strong computational and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance scored 20,088 points in Geekbench multi-core testing and demonstrated top-tier image processing performance alongside strong software compilation execution using Clang. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 249.73 GB/sec, while write throughput measured 102.08 GB/sec. PassMark CPU testing yielded 62,325.35 points, reinforced by robust vector and matrix instruction throughput via AMX and AVX-512. Static web throughput reached 78.25 GB/sec, while in-memory operations demonstrated 64.82 million Redis SET operations per second and steady prompt processing rates across small-to-medium language models.

By pairing 48 high-clock vCPUs with a trimmed 96 GB memory pool, the D48ls_v6 reduces memory overhead costs for workloads dominated by compute requirements rather than large in-memory working sets. However, the absence of local ephemeral NVMe disks means all persistent data transfers traverse network storage, introducing storage I/O considerations. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration and build pipelines, CPU-based matrix operations, web serving clusters, and distributed microservices where high core density is prioritized over expansive memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is an Intel-based virtual machine configured for compute-intensive tasks, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 260 MB L3 cache, the system incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong execution across multi-core workloads, Clang code compilation, large-block memory bandwidth, and static web serving, with Redis reaching 64.82 million SET operations per second. The server contains no local storage, requiring external premium disk volumes for persistent storage. Its resource profile offers high core density without the cost overhead of unneeded memory capacity, making it a viable platform for CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, image and video manipulation, and horizontally scalable web serving infrastructure.
